name: starter-web-app
title: Starter: Web App
description: The whole spine of a platform web-app in one command: a multi-stage Dockerfile with EXPOSE + HEALTHCHECK, a local docker-compose with a named volume, the ghcr build workflow gated on tests, an open /api/health, the standalone next.config, the verify script's config, and the doc set (00-map, decisions, gates). Pulls in the vitest/eslint/prettier configs, the rebuild-and-verify script and the no-emoji gate. Prisma is NOT assumed — the Dockerfile documents the three edits that add it.

files.content:
# Standard image for a Next.js App Router app on this platform: multi-stage, standalone output, a
# non-root user, an EXPOSEd port and a HEALTHCHECK the container runtime can actually read.
#
# Requires `output: 'standalone'` in next.config.ts (the starter ships that file too) — without it
# .next/standalone does not exist and the runtime stage copies nothing.

# ---------- deps ----------
FROM node:24-alpine AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci

# ---------- build ----------
FROM node:24-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
# The build stage has no .env, so a fail-fast env module (@thiengthb/lib-env) would abort `next build`
# on variables that only exist at run time. This is scoped to THIS stage — the runtime stage below is a
# separate FROM and never inherits it, which is what keeps the escape hatch out of production.
ENV SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=1
# The runtime stage copies ./public unconditionally, and a COPY of a missing path fails the whole
# build. Templates that scaffold a public/ make this a no-op; an app that has none would otherwise
# break here for a reason the error message does not explain.
RUN mkdir -p public && npm run build

# ---------- runtime ----------
FROM node:24-alpine
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
# tzdata so TZ actually applies — an app that computes "today" in local time needs it.
RUN apk add --no-cache tzdata

COPY --from=build /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=build /app/.next/static ./.next/static
COPY --from=build /app/public ./public

# App data lives in a named VOLUME mounted here, never in the image and never a bind mount
# (platform invariant: it must survive a rebuild and be movable between targets).
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node:node /data
ENV HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
ENV PORT=3000

USER node
EXPOSE 3000

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health || exit 1

CMD ["node", "server.js"]

# ---------- when you add Prisma ----------
# This base is deliberately Prisma-free so a fresh app builds and runs before it has a schema. Once
# `prisma/schema.prisma` exists, three edits make migrations apply on container start:
#
#   1. deps stage:     COPY prisma ./prisma      (before `npm ci`, so the postinstall sees it)
#   2. build stage:    RUN npx prisma generate && npm run build
#   3. a prisma-cli stage + a CMD that runs `prisma migrate deploy` before `exec node server.js`,
#      and `RUN apk add --no-cache openssl` in the runtime stage (the engine needs it on alpine).
#
# The worked version is `todo/Dockerfile` — copy from there rather than re-deriving it.

node_modules
.next
.git
.env
.env.*
*.log
coverage
test-results
playwright-report
docs
README.md
Dockerfile
.dockerignore
docker-compose*.yml

# Local run for `target: local` — the app is built here and published on a host port. No reverse proxy
# and no identity provider in front of it; "deploy" means rebuild the container and verify it healthy.
#
# The compose PROJECT name comes from this directory, so the volume below really lands as
# `<dirname>_app_data` — it already carries the app's name, and it is a named volume, never a bind mount.
services:
  app:
    build: .
    image: ${APP_NAME:-app}:local
    container_name: ${APP_NAME:-app}
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Pick a free port per app and pin it in .env — two local apps on 3000 is the usual collision.
      - '${HOST_PORT:-3000}:3000'
    environment:
      TZ: ${TZ:-Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh}
      # Secrets are read from .env (chmod 600, gitignored) — never written into this file.
    volumes:
      - app_data:/data
    # Runtime hardening. The image already runs as the non-root `node` user; these two close the paths
    # that let a compromised process regain what the user gave up. Both verified against this exact
    # image: a Next standalone server needs no Linux capability (it binds 3000, not a privileged port).
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    # read_only: true is the next step up. It WORKS on this image — measured 2026-07-30 with the three
    # lines below: container healthy, / and /api/health both 200, `echo x > /app/probe` refused, /data
    # and the tmpfs still writable, nothing in the log. It is opt-in rather than default because it is
    # verified against a BARE app: the first thing this starter tells you to add is Prisma, whose engine
    # and native modules may write outside /tmp, and that failure appears at run time, not build time.
    # Turn it on once the app's own dependencies are known, and re-verify:
    #   read_only: true
    #   tmpfs:
    #     - /tmp
    #     - /app/.next/cache   # Next's ISR + image-optimisation cache; tmpfs means it is lost on restart

volumes:
  app_data:

# Build the image in GitHub Actions and push it to ghcr.io. Nothing here deploys: the target pulls.
#
# The image name derives from the repository, so this file needs no editing when you copy it into a new
# repo. Tests gate the build — an image that fails its own suite never reaches the registry.
name: build-and-push

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Docs-only changes do not rebuild the image.
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'
      - 'docs/**'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least privilege by DEFAULT: without this block every job inherits the repository's default token
# scope, which on an older repo is read/write. The `test` job runs `npm ci`, i.e. arbitrary dependency
# postinstall scripts — it must not hold a token that can push. Jobs widen this individually.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}

concurrency:
  group: build-and-push
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      # npx, not `npm test`: a registry item cannot merge a script into package.json, so the
      # workflow must not assume one exists. Add "test": "vitest run" and use it if you prefer.
      - run: npx vitest run

  build:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=latest
            type=sha

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

# Per-repo config for scripts/rebuild-and-verify.sh. Keeping the values here means the script itself
# stays byte-identical to the registry copy, so a fix upstream is a re-add, not a merge.
SERVICE=app
BASE=http://localhost:3000
HEALTH=/api/health
EXPECT='"ok":true'
# Every route a user can reach. Add each new page here — a green build says nothing about whether a
# server component throws at render time.
ROUTES="/"
# Commands run by --gates. npx rather than npm scripts, so this works before package.json is edited.
GATE_CMDS="npm run lint|npx vitest run|npx prettier --check ."

## 8. Working here

```bash
npm run dev                          # localhost:3000
npx vitest run                       # tests (add "test": "vitest run" to package.json for `npm test`)
npx prettier --check .               # formatting (add "format:check" likewise)
bash scripts/rebuild-and-verify.sh   # rebuild the container and prove it serves
```

The two npm scripts above are the one thing `shadcn add` could not do for you: a registry item installs
files, and `package.json` is a file it must not overwrite. Add them once and forget it.
